Information since September points to a strengthening labor market and strong real activity, with PCE inflation near the FOMC’s symmetric 2% objective and longer-run expectations little changed. In line with Taylor-type policy guidance and the expectations-augmented Phillips curve (e.g., Clarida, Galí, and Gertler; Rudebusch and Svensson), such conditions warrant gradual rate increases to keep inflation anchored, consistent with the Fisher relation linking expected inflation and nominal rates. The Committee maintained the federal funds rate at 2 to 2.25% while continuing balance-sheet normalization in Treasuries and agency MBS—open market operations that transmit policy via reserves and term-premium channels—though it noted some moderation in business fixed investment, an IS-curve channel sensitive to interest rates. Net tone: positive growth outlook with balanced risks and a mildly hawkish policy bias.
